statement: Under the deterministic graph connectivity benchmark and training protocol used for Figure 2, a nonlinear RNN attains 100.00%, 98.60%, and 96.50% accuracy on lengths 1-100, 101-200, and 201-300, while Transformer, Mamba, RWKV-7, and DeltaNet attain the lower reported values; this empirical separation is attributed to the L-complete reachability computation.
quantifiers: The displayed accuracies concern one released training/evaluation protocol and three finite length ranges; the paper does not report seeds or uncertainty intervals.
blocker_after_route_1: The release audit establishes exact data and code defects but contains no faithful five-model training results. The public release has no dependency lock or usable commands, provides no seeds or Figure 2 logs, and its sole DGC checkpoint is a self-attention model mislabeled as an RNN checkpoint.
blocker_after_route_3: Three distinct routes establish that the release is defective, its only checkpoint diverges sharply from Figure 2, and repairing the generator removes the exact endpoint shortcut. None identifies the unavailable Figure 2 seeds, checkpoints, executable environment, or one consistent five-model protocol. Confidence remains LOW, so the dedicated falsification route is mandatory.
limitations: Route 1 is an exact audit of the public release, not a neural training reproduction and not a falsification of the displayed numerical results.
